postUpgradeTasks.description:
Regenerate terraform.md after a dependency bump. The Modules table renders each module's `?ref=<sha>` in its Version column, so a bare terraform-modules digest bump staleness the doc without touching a variable, output or resource (#26, four module blocks). Since this repo gained PR CI -- which runs .pre-commit-config.yaml verbatim, including a terraform-docs hook that WRITES -- that drift is no longer merely invisible, it is a red check on every such PR. Renovate cannot infer the docs change, so the generator has to re-run.

The command must match the allowlist regex in the shared renovate.yml workflow's `allowed_commands` byte for byte: postUpgrade shell is refused unless the SELF-HOSTED (global) config allowlists it, and a repo's renovate.json cannot authorize its own commands. That default allowlist has always named this exact path; the script is what was missing here.

fileFilters names the file rather than a `**/` glob because this repo is a single root module with exactly one terraform.md. executionMode is `branch`: the script regenerates the whole root module whatever changed, so once per branch is strictly cheaper than once per upgrade on a grouped PR.

customManagers.description: terraform-docs, in the two places that pin it. These MUST move together: CI runs the pre-commit hook and fails on any file it rewrites, while ci/renovate-terraform-docs.sh is what generates the file being checked -- so a skew between them fails every Renovate PR on a docs diff nobody wrote. Nothing tracked either pin before: the pre-commit manager reads remote `repo:` entries, not a local hook's docker_image, and the docker managers are not enabled here. The script also asserts the two agree at runtime, so a regex that stops matching fails loudly instead of silently generating the wrong format.
